To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) a nonlinear filtering approach to motion and structure estimation is possible, and that (ii) it can be implemented in real time.

1) a causal algorithm for the estimation of three-dimensional structure and motion from a sequence can be implemented in real time; 2) the algorithm is stable and robust to noise; 3) the algorithm can be used to recover the motion of objects that occlude each other; 4) the algorithm can handle uncalibrated cameras; and 5) the implementation of the algorithm is available for public testing.
(1) the problem of motion and structure from 2-D images can be solved in the causal setting; and (2) a practical implementation of this solution can be achieved.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an algorithm and its implementation for estimating three-dimensional motion and structure from a sequence of monocular images.
a fundamental issue of computer vision: the causal estimation of the three-dimensional motion and structure of a scene from two-dimensional images.
the development of a theory and an implementation of a causal algorithm for estimating 3-D motion and structure from 2-D image sequences.
